document.title: Tighten the review layout
document.summary: Why, What, and Look for stop near 68 characters. Sources use the full brief width. The header and the overview kicker share one file count. A skipped binary is a grey line on the overview, and only when a file was skipped. A one-file group has no file rail. Hunk blocks are rounded, with no shadow. A multi-file rail is narrower.
document.why: [This session](source:s1) asks to apply the approved audit to the fixed review UI.

sources.label: Cursor session · Sep 26
sources.gist: Implement the approved audit: cap the brief, drop the single-file rail, flatten hunk cards, align the file count, and tighten the multi-file rail. Keep the story boxes and only lower their tint.

parts.name: Review layout
parts.summary: The fixed review UI caps the brief, aligns the file count, and gives the diff the width the file rail was using.

groups.title: Brief, sources, and the file count
groups.why: [This session](source:s1) asks to cap the brief, put a kind on each source, and show one file total. A skipped binary is named on the overview.
groups.summary: The brief measure wraps Why, What, and Look for. Sources use the full brief width. The overview kicker and the header reading mark both use the grouped file paths. A skipped binary is a grey line under that kicker.

groups.title: File rail and hunk rows
groups.why: [This session](source:s1) asks to drop the rail for one file, start it collapsed under about 1100px, and keep hunks as rounded blocks.
groups.summary: A group with one file renders the hunk alone. A wider multi-file group keeps a narrower rail. Hunk blocks are rounded and have a border, with no shadow. The active file's border is primary only when another file is in the group.
lookFor: Subtle. Under 1099px the rail starts collapsed only when storage has no choice. A stored open value, or ?rail=open, keeps the rail open.

commits.subject: Drop the hunk count, give sources the brief width, and round hunk blocks.
commits.author: Cursor Agent
commits.body:
The header no longer reports grouped hunks. A skipped binary is a grey line on the overview, and only when a file was skipped. The 68-character measure stays on Why, What, and Look for. Hunk blocks are rounded again, with a border and no shadow.

Co-authored-by: Máté Molnár <matemolnar8@users.noreply.github.com>
